兼 brings two or more functions or posts together. 兼ねる かねる can describe a room serving two purposes or a person holding two posts. 兼任 けんにん specifically concerns holding concurrent posts. Concurrent roles need not involve performing two actions at exactly the same moment.

～かねる, usually written in kana after a verb's masu stem: 同意しかねる (どういしかねる) — cannot agree; a difficulty/inability construction, not literal combining

The two kun entries share the pronunciation かねる but describe different constructions. Practise one reading key, not two independent readings. For the suffix, 同意する becomes 同意し + かねる; do not attach it to the dictionary form or the て-form. It is negative in meaning without ない. The separate ～かねない pattern means "might," not simply "can." The linked article explains both uses and their examples.

兼任 けんにん — holding concurrent posts
Between role or function names, 兼 (けん) can mean "also serving as": 首相兼外相 (しゅしょうけんがいしょう) is a prime minister also serving as foreign minister. It is not a general replacement for と or English "and."
Dictionaries also record a separate "beforehand" branch, as in 兼題 (けんだい), a poetry topic announced before the meeting. Do not force the concurrent-role translation onto every compound.
Compare 典 and 具, which have spreading feet below their upper boxes. 曲 has a divided enclosure, without 兼's long central vertical strokes and spreading lower strokes.

兼 concerns combining or serving in more than one capacity; ねる completes the native verb. The ordinary combined-role verb is written 兼ねる. The difficulty suffix is usually written in kana as ～かねる; its meaning is not obtained by translating the kanji literally.

兼任する (けんにんする) describes holding concurrent posts. 勤める (つとめる) means to work for or be employed, not specifically to combine positions. ～できない also expresses inability, but ～かねる is useful for difficulty or reluctance in formal responses; it is not a universal replacement in every inability sentence.

兼任 けんにん — holding concurrent posts
兼任 means one person holding two or more posts or duties concurrently. Use 兼任する as a verb, marking the post or posts with を: an additional post, or two posts joined with と.
首相が外相を兼任しています。 (しゅしょうががいしょうをけんにんしています。) — The prime minister also serves as foreign minister.
彼女は社長と会長を兼任しています。 (かのじょはしゃちょうとかいちょうをけんにんしています。) — She holds both the president's and the chairperson's positions.
These are overlapping appointments, not necessarily two tasks performed at the same instant.

兼 contributes combining or serving concurrently; 任 contributes a post or duty. The modifier 兼 describes how the posts are held. The on readings are ケン + ニン. This explains the compound's meaning, not the historical origin of either character.

兼ねる (かねる) also describes combining posts, but extends to combined functions, such as a room serving two purposes. 兼務 (けんむ) is a close synonym for carrying out concurrent duties. 専任 (せんにん), dedicated service in a particular post or duty, is the contrast.

就任 (しゅうにん) means taking office. It marks entry into a post, not the continued holding of two posts. Compare the particles: 社長に就任する (しゃちょうにしゅうにんする), "take office as president," but 外相を兼任する (がいしょうをけんにんする), "also serve as foreign minister."

The point is that one person has multiple roles. Two colleagues sharing one job do not establish 兼任 merely by sharing it. Nor does ordinary employment by itself imply concurrent posts: 勤める (つとめる) can simply mean working for an employer.
